properties.name: Two releases looked complete and shipped no container image — the cut verifies ASSETS off the release object, and the image is not an asset
properties.statement:
MEASURED across the v0.60.0 and v0.60.1 cuts. Both were tagged, both published all five release assets, both read `draft: false` — and NEITHER published a container image.

🛑 THE RELEASE OBJECT DID NOT LIE. It was complete, for the assets. The image is not an asset and never appears there, so the standing check — "verify the release published, don't trust the workflow's green", which the cut already does — cannot see it. A cut that passes that check has verified everything except the one artefact a container consumer pulls.

WHAT TO ADD, at the same point the assets are verified:

    gh run view <run> --json jobs --jq '.jobs[] | "\(.conclusion)\t\(.name)"'

The `container image` job must read `success`. Its last step prints
`published <IMAGE>:<VERSION>` after an `imagetools inspect`, so the log carries
the confirmation directly.

⚠️ TWO TRAPS INSIDE THAT, both met on 2026-09-14:
 · THE RUN'S OWN CONCLUSION IS USELESS HERE IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. A run reads RED while the assets published fine, because the container job fails AFTER `publish release` has succeeded. Read the JOB.
 · THE IMAGE NAME IS `ghcr.io/<owner>/<repo>/reflow2-mcp`, not `ghcr.io/<owner>/reflow2-mcp`. The shorter guess 404s and is indistinguishable from a missing image — which is how a successful publish was nearly reported as a failure minutes after the real one.

⭐ THE GATE WAS RIGHT ALL THREE TIMES and must not be blamed: the smoke test runs BEFORE the push, so both failures refused to ship an unverified image rather than shipping one. The capability held. What failed was a new check inside it, and the CUT had no step that would notice the difference between "no image was built" and "no image was published".

📌 THE GENERAL SHAPE, and it is the same one `rule:success-is-read-from-the-authoritative-object` already states on three other surfaces: an object can be complete about what it covers and silent about what it does not, and the silence reads as consent. The assets object is authoritative for assets only.
